text.p: These are the leading stories in the Namibian press on Monday.
Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
- Emergency plans to build a 250 km pipeline to link Namibia's central areas to the Okavango river by next year, are likely to be shelved if the country continues to receive good rains.
- President Sam Nujoma has sent his personal doctor to investigate allegations of an illegal, insanitary seal meat operation at Henties Bay.
- Namibia can only expect a modest economic growth rate of two percent in 1997, says Bank of Windhoek economist Emile van Zyl.
- The fate of the Cessna 210, missing since last Thursday with five people on board, is still unclear despite an extensive search operation over the weekend.
- The continued search for a Cecssna 210, missing since last Thursday, was unsuccesful on Sunday.
- Namibia's emergency plan to pump water from the Okavango river to the central areas of the country will be put on hold for the time being.
